findings: claude-cli (oauth_token, in container): all nine mandatory probes pass on the pinned image sha256:f642e03d19ba… over the qualified egress profile. cancel_tree: docker stop (SIGTERM through --init) ended a running Bash turn in under a second with exit 143. crash_recovery: SIGKILL (exit 137) mid-turn, then --resume with the exact prior session id answered from that session's history.
filesystem_containment: root read-only, /workspace the only writable bind, no /Users, no docker socket, /root read-only and empty, uid 65534; the turn wrote only .probe (the probe's own file).

codex-cli: not run in the container. The ChatGPT-account credential lives in ~/.codex on the host and the agent does not copy it; the user runs scripts/sandbox_up.sh --codex-home DIR, then scripts/container_qualify.py --driver codex --codex-home DIR. Until then the Work 015 host-side result (4/9) stands.
container image tools are newer than the host binaries (claude 2.1.278 vs host 2.1.267); the pin that matters is the image digest.

secret_isolation: the OAuth token is absent from the stream, stderr, workspace, sidecar log, argv and the worker-owned session home. It is present in the container's environment by construction (the CLI needs it); docker inspect on the host can read it, which is host authority, not agent-visible output. A credential broker (V3-022) remains the production answer.
trust class: artifacts are admitted as operator trust (this session measured and graded them). They are not an independent verifier result; the human cutover gate (V3-062) still applies.
review R1 (contract lens): cancel_tree now also requires exit code 143 (SIGTERM honoured) so a container that died for another reason within the window cannot pass.
method: scripts/container_qualify.py: real turns inside the pinned image on the qualified egress profile; QualificationRunner with CAS-admitted artifacts (operator trust: self-measured, not an independent verifier); status fail unless all nine pass
